name: Digit lines from a glyph table

atomicDiscipline.rule: Run exactly the printed hypothesis. If the attempted change fails, degrades, or suggests a different fix, revert to the checkpoint and finish this experiment as failure. Start a new experiment for the next idea.

hypothesisMarkdown:
## Digit lines from a glyph table

Mechanism: lay out a one-font line of number characters (digits . , - + : %) by adding up per-character glyphs and advances taken from Core Text once per (font, size), after checking the table against Core Text on all character pairs and 138 random lines. Allowed: gpui_macos text_system.rs. Forbidden: any other shaping path.
measurementPlanMarkdown: Run text-relabel, table-stream, dashboard-clock, data-table, text-typing against the E9 results (3 reps), then A/B inside one binary with an environment switch. Pass: shaping cost down on text-relabel and data-table, no scenario slower.

measurements.delta: -32% (not reproduced in-binary: the machine locked before it could be repeated)

measurements.metric: table-stream on CPU, same binary, table on vs off

reportMarkdown:
## Digit lines from a glyph table Finished

Passed: false. The table verifies against Core Text (new test passed) but composing a line is not cheaper than Core Text's warm path (1.8 us either way in a microbenchmark), and alternating the same binary with the table on and off showed table-stream 18% slower with it. The earlier text-relabel gain over E9 is therefore drift between builds, not this change. Reverted. The Mac's screen locked at about 21:00, after which no window could be drawn, so further benchmark runs wait for an unlock.

Attempt Count: 1. Out-of-scope changes: none.
decisionMarkdown:
### Decision

Reverted failure. Lesson recorded: cross-build comparisons drift by up to 10% in the cheap scenarios; alternate one binary with an environment switch to confirm a small effect.
